Windows Firewall may be blocking your phone

Allow it once so phones on your network can reach this PC.

Windows Firewall is blocking all incoming connections

Phones can't reach this PC while that's on. Open Windows Security → Firewall & network protection, click your active network and untick Block all incoming connections. On a work or school PC this may be set by your administrator.

Scanned the code but nothing loads?

  • Put the phone on the same Wi-Fi as this PC — not mobile data or a guest network.
  • Click Allow through firewall below, then scan again.
  • Try another address under the QR code: this PC has more than one network adapter, and a VPN or virtual adapter may have been picked first.
  • Turn off any VPN on the PC or phone, and any third-party antivirus firewall for a moment.
  • Some routers keep devices apart (“AP isolation” or “client isolation”), as do most work, school, hotel and guest networks. To check, turn on the phone's Personal Hotspot, join it from this PC, and scan the new code.

Setup & settings

Start with Windows Runs quietly in the tray so your phone can connect any time you open it.
Keep running when this window is closed The controller stays plugged in; reopen this window from the tray icon.
Phone can't connect? Lets phones on your network through Windows Firewall (asks for permission).
Updates Checks for a newer version by itself every few hours.
Test vibration Buzzes every connected phone the way a game's rumble would.
Tips & troubleshooting
  • The phone and this PC must be on the same Wi-Fi. Guest networks usually block it.
  • Windows' “Game Controllers” panel (joy.cpl) lists this pad but won't show it moving — it reads the old DirectInput API, which Xbox controllers (real ones too) don't use. Games, Steam and the drawing above read XInput.
  • The Guide button reaches Steam and the Xbox Game Bar; most games don't see it, same as a real Xbox controller.
  • Rumble needs an Android phone: iPhone browsers don't allow web pages to vibrate.
